title: Wall Street Journal EMP explanation for Malmstrom
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Wall Street Journal EMP explanation for Malmstrom, about 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And cut back to uh a year or two ago, the Wall Street Journal reports this clearly disinfo hit piece on UFOs and it's around this event and they say that an EMP in 1967
They said that they wheeled an EMP up to the base and fried all the electronics on site with people present.
tellings.difference: Adds that the EMP device was said to have been wheeled up to the base and fried the electronics with people present.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the recent Wall Street Journal article that blamed the 1967 Malmstrom shutdown on an EMP.

as_told.title: Wall Street Journal article blaming Malmstrom on an EMP test

tellings.quote: ridiculous Wall Street Journal uh piece comes out by this guy named Joel Shectman.
tellings.difference: Names the author, Joel Shectman, links Sean Kirkpatrick to the piece and dates it to 2025.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the Wall Street Journal piece that blamed the Malmstrom missile shutdown on an EMP and that Michels calls a hit piece.

as_told.title: Wall Street Journal EMP article on Malmstrom

tellings.quote: So anyways, this Wall Street Journal reporter named Joel Schechtman writes that this was all a secret EMP or electromagnetic pulse experiment, seeing if the US could shut down our own nukes with people present as if that's not incredibly dangerous and reckless and has any precedent.
tellings.difference: Adds that the host called it dangerous, reckless and without precedent.
tellings.link_reason: Both are the WSJ claim that the 1967 Malmstrom shutdown was a secret EMP experiment, in Schechtman's article.

as_told.title: WSJ claim that Malmstrom was a secret EMP experiment

tellings.quote: He was this probably the sole source for this sloppily written Wall Street Journal article that uh poorly explained away a bunch of UFO incidents around Malmstrom nuclear base in 1967 calling it the product of a a non-nuclear EMP,
tellings.difference: Calls Kirkpatrick probably the sole source for the article and calls the EMP non-nuclear.
tellings.link_reason: Both are the Wall Street Journal article that explained the 1967 Malmstrom incidents as an EMP test, with Kirkpatrick linked to it.

as_told.title: WSJ article explains away the 1967 Malmstrom UFO incidents, with Kirkpatrick as likely source

related.note: The Wall Street Journal explains the same 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown as an EMP rather than a UFO, a competing core claim about the same event.

Both are about EMP testing on missile equipment as an explanation for the shutdowns. The WSJ account says an EMP was wheeled up to Malmstrom itself; Salas says such testing was done only at SAMSO and Hill AFB, not at operational bases.
Salas's rebuttal disputes the WSJ claim that an EMP test caused the 1967 Malmstrom shutdowns; it is a competing account of the same event.

plain: In 1967, at Malmstrom, an Air Force base in Montana that housed nuclear missiles, others tell of missiles being shut down while a glowing object hovered nearby. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that a Wall Street Journal article, written by a reporter named Joel Shectman and linked by Michels to a man named Sean Kirkpatrick, explained the event as a test of an EMP, a burst of electromagnetic energy that can fry electronics. As Michels retells it, the article said the device was wheeled up to the base and knocked out the electronics with people present, and he calls the piece a deliberate disinformation hit job.
